ee190bd8610c: OPEN-NPU explores distributed scientific computing using NPUs on campus and volunteer computers.
5a6bc34923e4: OPEN-NPU explores how research teams can pool the neural processing units (NPUs) of volunteer computers to run scientific workloads in batches.
b99fdacc7af0: The team describes its research objective, data type, and planned computations. Once the project is approved, the team receives an API key.
b562c8dde282: Windows agents claim batches that their NPUs can run. Each agent executes a predefined computational graph. If a node disconnects, another can pick up its batch.
fdfb5a70c564: The API reports progress and returns results in submission order. Multiple computers can process independent batches in parallel.
630b2be795b3: An open pilot for research teams.
814653ba5503: The local prototype validates a demo workload on Intel AI Boost, from submission to result retrieval.
3b592f400963: For the first use case, we are looking for repeatable tasks that are easy to distribute and whose results can be checked against a reference. Running inference on batches of microscopy images is one possibility.
e45ba4a70de0: Research teams can propose a workload. IT and research computing teams can identify compatible computers for a future interinstitutional pilot.
5eb5b84ff820: Describe the use case, the estimated workload, and how you would validate the results. If you can contribute hardware, include the number of computers and their NPU models.
5acae8c5d781: This form collects a description of the project. Avoid including confidential research data.
landing.workload: Describe the research need, estimated workload, and how you will verify the results.
landing.contribution-info: Tell us what computers your institution could make available. The pilot team will contact you to check compatibility and organise a trial.
docs.demo-prerequisites: You need an API key for an approved project and a compatible NPU agent available to that project.
docs.demo-result: The script submits three values, waits for completion, and checks that the result is [4, 9, 16].
landing.llm-title: Split an LLM across multiple NPUs
landing.llm-intro: Independent tasks run in parallel batches. To distribute inference for a single language model, OPEN-NPU runs its stages in sequence on compatible nodes.
landing.llm-export: The team splits and exports the model as OpenVINO graphs. Each stage must fit within the resources of the computer running it.
landing.llm-sign: The versioned capsule describes the stages and their inputs and outputs. Once it is approved, agents verify its signature and file integrity.
landing.llm-run: The server assigns each stage to a compatible node and passes its output to the next stage. A stage can be reassigned if its lease expires.
landing.llm-validation: The prototype was tested with a miniature decoder on Intel AI Boost. Each pretrained LLM needs a suitable partition and validation on the target hardware.
landing.agent-description: Download the Windows x64 agent. Ask the pilot team for an invitation to enroll a new computer.
landing.agent-update-info: Extract the archive. For a signed release, first verify it using a separately obtained verifier and the publisher fingerprint. The update preserves enrollment and preferences.
landing.agent-trust: For the first signed update, also pass the publisher’s SHA-256 fingerprint as shown below.
Aucun téléchargement disponible sur cett: No download is available on this instance.
landing.agent-auto: Starting with version 0.3.5, the installed agent checks for updates every 24 hours. It downloads the new release and notifies you in Windows when it is ready to install.
landing.agent-public: Install the Windows x64 agent without an invitation. Your computer appears in the fleet and can contribute after an administrator approves it.
